purpose: Granisetron is used to prevent and treat nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery. It is very helpful for people going through cancer treatments who experience severe nausea. It does not treat nausea from motion sickness or the stomach flu.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called serotonin during chemotherapy or surgery, which can trigger the vomiting center in your brain and gut, making you feel very sick. Granisetron works by blocking the specific spots (called 5-HT3 receptors) where serotonin would normally attach and cause nausea. By blocking those spots, the signal to feel sick is stopped before it can start.
common_side_effects: Headache is the most common side effect. You may also notice constipation, tiredness, or dizziness. Some people feel weak or have mild stomach discomfort. These effects are usually mild and temporary.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have a heart rhythm problem or are taking other medications, as granisetron can rarely affect your heart's electrical rhythm. Let your healthcare team know all medications you take, including herbal supplements. If you develop severe stomach pain or bloating, contact your doctor right away. Avoid it if you have had an allergic reaction to it before.
typical_dosing: For chemotherapy nausea, it is often taken as a tablet (1 mg twice daily or 2 mg once daily) starting the day of treatment. It also comes as a patch (Sancuso) worn on the upper arm, applied 24 to 48 hours before chemotherapy. An injectable form is given by a nurse in the clinic before your treatment begins. Your doctor will choose the form and dose that is best for you.
